title: Delegated Tenant Isolation Sandboxes and Surge Simulation PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Provide a controlled, tenant-scoped sandbox environment and an automated surge-simulation harness for Dedicated deployments. This PRD defines a feature that lets platform customers and Redwood SREs create ephemeral isolation sandboxes that mirror a tenant's runtime configuration (model variants, routing policies, CPU/GPU reservation) and then run synthetic surge/traffic scenarios to verify graceful fallback, preemption, and tenant-level shaping policies without impacting production traffic.
problem_statement: Operators lack a safe way to validate tenant isolation and fallback behavior for Dedicated capacity before real traffic hits the system. Incidents surface where tenant SLOs are violated during bursts or noisy neighbors because configuration interactions (routing fallbacks + soft preemption rules + tenant quotas) weren't tested at scale. This increases toil for SREs and reduces trust from enterprise customers that need predictable isolation guarantees.
goals: 1) Ship an ephemeral tenant sandbox that reproduces a customer's Dedicated runtime configuration. 2) Provide a surge-simulation harness that can run configurable traffic patterns (spike, ramp, sustained) against the sandbox. 3) Produce human- and machine-readable reports that map observed behavior to policy surfaces (shaping, throttles, preemption). 4) Enable non-destructive canary exercises for rollout validation of isolation-related config changes.
non_goals: This PRD does not include long-term UI polish for the Console (v1 API + basic console controls only). It also does not replace the production autoscaler; simulations should not trigger cluster-wide autoscaling in production regions (simulator will run on dedicated test capacity).
requirements: A reproducible sandbox creator API: submit tenant config (model versions, routing, quotas, region) -> returns sandbox_id with immutable runtime snapshot
Sandbox supports a copy of tenant-level routing policies and fallback chains but with traffic redirected to isolated test hosts
A surge-simulation engine with generative load patterns: spike, linear ramp, pulse, and mixed tenant blends
Test harness must be able to run variable request sizes (token counts), sequence lengths, and concurrency to exercise batching/kv cache behavior
Telemetry export: simulated traces, token-level latency, queue lengths, batch sizes, preemption events, and quota-exhaustion markers
A report generator that maps failures to policy triggers (e.g., 'soft-preempt invoked after 12s of sustained high-priority usage')
Minimal Console integration: start sandbox, select traffic template, run simulation, view report (read-only for v1)
Access controls: only tenant admin + Redwood SREs can create sandboxes; sandbox lifecycle must expire automatically
Simulation must run on isolated test pools and must not consume customer-reserved production capacity
Rollout hooks for canary: allow config diffing and a dry-run validation with pass/fail signal for automated rollouts
constraints: Simulators must not influence production autoscaler or billing systems. Hardware required for realistic GPU inference at scale is limited; initial rollout will use scaled-down token-rate equivalents and modeling to extrapolate to larger workloads. Timebox: MVP in 6 weeks of engineering investment.
assumptions: 1) We can reuse existing snapshot/serialization of tenant routing configs. 2) Dedicated test pools are available and can be reserved for simulation runs. 3) Accurate instrumentation exists in the serving runtime to surface preemption and queueing events.
user_flows: Tenant admin requests sandbox via API or Console -> submits configuration snapshot -> system provisions sandbox_id -> user chooses 'surge template' and run duration -> simulation runs -> report generated and downloadable
SRE triggers a sandbox for a problematic tenant -> runs a blended-noise simulation to reproduce a reported incident -> uses report to tune tenant shaping parameters
Product team includes sandbox validation step in rollout pipeline -> automated dry-run fails the rollout if isolation regressions detected
acceptance_criteria: Sandbox API can be used to provision and deprovision an environment within < 3 minutes for small configs
Simulation engine runs configured patterns and emits a report within 30 minutes for a standard 5-minute test with 3x synthetic load
Reports include token-level P50/P95/P99 latency, batch size distribution, number of preemption events, and quota saturation timestamps
No production capacity autoscaler events are triggered by simulator runs in any environment
Access control prevents non-authorized users from creating sandboxes; audit logs show creator and sandbox lifecycle events
Two internal validation runs conducted reproducing at least one historical incident pattern and producing actionable config diffs
success_metrics: Reduction in post-deploy isolation incidents for Dedicated customers by 40% within 3 months
Number of sandbox runs per month (target 50 internal + 20 customer-led in quarter 1 post-release)
Median time for SRE to triage noisy neighbor incidents reduces from 4 hours to 90 minutes when using sandbox reports
% of Dedicated rollouts that include sandbox dry-run checks reaches 60% within two release cycles
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): API + CLI + minimal Console controls, internal SRE-only access. Phase 2: gated customer beta for enterprise tenants with support access. Phase 3: public self-serve in Console with templated traffic profiles and billing controls. Each phase to be accompanied by runbooks and 2-week pilot campaigns with selected customers.
monitoring_and_alerting: Simulator metrics emitted to internal observability: simulation_run.started, simulation_run.completed, simulation_run.failed, preemption.events.count, batch.dist.percentiles. Alerts: simulation_run.failed > 3 in 24h, preemption.events spike during test runs (investigate sandbox contamination).
dependencies_notes: Depends on ENG to expose immutable tenant config snapshot API (re-use feature-branch created for PM-27109). Needs extra test-capacity provisioning from infra (ticketed with ENG-ops). Security sign-off required for sandbox network isolation (see security_review_required).
engineering_notes: Implementation should reuse existing runtime instrumentation for preemption and batch telemetry. For realistic GPU behavior, use a mix of reduced-concurrency real runs + synthetic amplification (token-rate multipliers) and a calibration step that maps reduced runs to full-scale expectations. Include telemetry hooks for later ML-based anomaly detection.
open_questions: What is the target scale (qps and concurrent requests) for beta customers vs internal SRE runs?
Should simulation runs be billable to customers or covered under enterprise support for beta?
Can we guarantee zero blast radius for every config (network/storage differences between sandbox and prod)?
Do we need a UI for editing traffic templates or rely on JSON templates in v1?
